class.name: WarmPolicy
class.brief_description: Strategy for deciding how each table pre-loads into a write-behind cache.
class.description:
Assign it to [member NetwDatabase.warm_policy]. The database walks the registered schema at init and asks the policy for one [WarmRequest] per table, then hands the batch to the backend. A plain [WarmPolicy] warms EVERYTHING, and it is what [member NetwDatabase.warm_policy] holds by default, so a write-behind backend pre-loads the whole open slot before the first read. Warming nothing is a [code]null[/code] policy, not a bare one: the two are different answers and the class carries only the first. Subclass it and override [method _plan_table] to narrow that default. An override that answers [code]null[/code] for a table leaves that table on the warm-everything answer, so a policy states only what it changes. [codeblock] # A policy that warms only the players table and leaves the rest lazy. class_name WarmPlayersOnly extends WarmPolicy
func _plan_table(table: StringName, _columns: Array[StringName]) -> WarmRequest: return WarmRequest.all() if table == &"players" else WarmRequest.none() [/codeblock]

method.name: _plan_table
method.description: Override to return the [WarmRequest] for [param table] given its declared [param columns]. Answer [method WarmRequest.none] to leave a table lazy; answering [code]null[/code] is not a way to abstain from warming, because the warm-everything default is what stands when this answers nothing. This is the override point only. Callers ask [method plan_table], which is what dispatches here.

method.name: plan_table
method.description: Returns the [WarmRequest] this policy plans for [param table] given its declared [param columns], which is [method WarmRequest.all] unless [method _plan_table] answers otherwise. Called once per registered table when the database initializes its backend. Synchronous backends ignore the result, so a policy can never break a read.
